Title: c. New Job Descriptions: Boys Volleyball Coach & Assistant

fields.Content: For the first time, the Grandview C-4 School District will sponsor a boys volleyball team during the spring semester.  As part of this exciting new opportunity for our students, we are seeking to hire both a Head Boys Volleyball Coach and an Assistant Volleyball Coach. These positions will play a critical role in establishing and developing the program, fostering athletic skills, teamwork, and sportsmanship among our student-athletes. The coaches will be responsible for planning and leading practices, developing game strategies, and promoting a positive, inclusive team environment. We look forward to building a successful program that provides additional extracurricular opportunities for our students and enhances their overall educational experience.
Approve the job description for the Head Boys Volleyball and Assistant Coach positions.

Head Coaching position pay range $6,584-$7,819
Assistant Coach position pay range $3,704-4,938

Title: d. New Job Description: Summer School Supervisor

fields.Content: Human Resources is recommending the addition of a new position titled Summer School Supervisor to support the effective planning and implementation of our summer school programs. This role will provide dedicated leadership and oversight, ensuring the delivery of high-quality instruction, smooth daily operations, and a safe, structured learning environment for all students and staff during the summer session. The Summer School Supervisor will work closely with building administrators, teachers, and support staff to address student needs, manage logistics, and support academic achievement. This position is intended to strengthen the overall effectiveness and consistency of our summer programming across the district.
Approve the job description for the Summer School Supervisor.

Senate Bill 711, which became effective August 28, 2008, contains a provision whereby the district must project estimated, non-binding, tax levy rates to be submitted to the County Clerk by April 8 of each year.

Effective January 1, 2009, per Section 137.180 RSMo, in a year the assessor increases the valuation of real property, the county clerk on or before March 15 shall send estimated assessed valuation amounts to the school district that is in a county with a charter form of government, other than any county adopting a charter form of government after January 1, 2008, (Jackson, Jefferson, St. Charles, and St. Louis Counties). Each school district shall then calculate and submit an estimated non-binding property tax rate to the county clerk's office by April 8 in odd-numbered years, as required by Section 137.243, RSMo. (ATT 1)

This is a reassessment year within Jackson County and the district recently received preliminary assessed valuation (AV) information.  The preliminary AV within the district increased from $791,686,709 to $883,926,318.

Based on the preliminary assessed valuation provided by Jackson County, the computed maximum Operating tax rate ceiling is $4.3987 per $100 AV.

The Debt Service calculated ceiling is $1.8358; however, Administration is recommending a voluntary reduction by the school district of .4692 and approval of an estimated 2025 tax levy rate of $1.3666 per $100 AV for debt service.

Approve an estimated tax levy rate of $4.3897 per $100 AV for General and Teacher (Combined) Operating Funds, and $1.3666 for the Debt Service Fund, for a total estimated tax levy rate of $5.7563 for 2025.

The Board of Education is requested to approve the procurement of two new upgraded firewalls and related services under the E-Rate program. This upgrade is essential to strengthening the district’s network security, enhancing data protection, and ensuring compliance with cybersecurity best practices.

A competitive bidding process was conducted, and Yellow Dog Networks was the sole bidder. Their proposal met all technical and security requirements, with a total project cost of $32,966. This includes $28,892 for the firewall equipment and $4,074 for Threat Prevention Services, which are not covered by E-Rate. The district’s portion of the cost is $9,852.40. The pricing falls within the expected range, ensuring a cost-effective and robust security solution for the district.

Approval of this item will allow the district to proceed with implementation, improving the reliability and safety of the network infrastructure.

E-rate funding will be requested to fund the project.  The District will request that e-rate pay 80% of the eligible portion of the project and the district’s portion is 20% which will be covered by the technology plan.
Approve a purchase from Yellow Dog Networks for an amount not to exceed $32,966 pending E-rate funding approval.
Budgeted

Grandview C-4 will apply for e-rate funding to help offset the costs associated with the purchase of annual maintenance for district network equipment including switches, wireless access points, and controllers.  As part of the e-rate process an Form 470 was posted on the Schools and Library Programs site which vendors across the country have access to bid on.   One vendor, Aercor, submitted a proposal.  Aercor is our current vendor and pricing is aligned with what should be expected for maintenance. The Bid Evaluation Matrix (Attachment #1) is included for your review.

Based on the bid evaluation, which is based upon cost of eligible goods and services, we are recommending Aercor.

The request includes maintenance for 524 access points, 2 Wireless Controllers, and 126 switches which are currently installed at the district.

The proposed cost will be $25,876.82 before the e-rate discount.  We anticipate an e-rate discount of 80% for the 2025-26 funding year.  The cost after e-rate discount is estimated to be $5,175.36.
Approve the proposal presented by Aercor for an amount not to exceed $25,876.82 before e-rate discount.

Grandview C-4 has applied for e-rate funding to help offset the costs associated with our Wide Area Network (WAN) service.  This board item requests approval of the annual renewal payment.

Based on the bid evaluation, which includes cost of eligible goods and services, experience with the district, implementation plan, RFP response, and cost of eligible products, we are recommending AT&T.

The WAN connects each school site to the district network. Our current solution selected would provide a 10 gig connection over 5 years.  There are 4 more years in the contract. 

The WAN service will cost $110,351.76 per year, before the e-rate discount.  We anticipate an e-rate discount of 80% for the 2025-26 funding year.  The annual cost for the district, after e-rate discount, is estimated to be $22,070.35.

The term of the contract is three (5) years.  We are in the 2nd year of the contract.  E-rate funding has to be re-applied for each year.

Approve the annual agreement with AT&T for WAN services contract for an amount not to exceed $110,351.76 per year before e-rate discount. We anticipate our annual after e-rate discount cost to be $22,070.35.
With e-rate funding – Estimated $22,070.35 annually (without e-rate funding - $110,351.76 annually)

As technology needs increase, it is important to provide a high quality infrastructure to meet the needs of our district.  Therefore, it is necessary to upgrade the cabling in support of current and future technology implementations. 

The district will install new data network cabling to each classroom and work space in district elementary schools to support instruction and management of the school.  This new cabling will modernize the cabling system for the sites.

Four bidders presented proposals, Uplink, Envision Technology Group, Supernal Systems, LLC and Yellow Dog Networks .  The best bid was from Yellow Dog Networks Networks at $129,310.  The district portion will be $25,862.  Yellow Dog Networks/Pangea is a vendor who works with the district on a regular basis.  

E-rate funding will be requested to fund the project.  The District will request that e-rate pay 80% of the project and the district’s portion is 20% which will be covered by the technology plan.
Approve a purchase from Yellow Dog Networks Network for an amount not to exceed $129,310  pending E-rate funding approval.

The Board of Education is requested to approve the procurement of 5G WiFi equipment and service for 37 school buses under the E-Rate program. This initiative will enhance student access to digital resources during transit, supporting academic engagement and connectivity for students who rely on school transportation. Additionally, the upgraded WiFi service will assist the Transportation Department by enabling the use of innovative software and hardware resources to efficiently manage the district fleet.

A competitive bidding process was conducted in compliance with E-Rate guidelines, with proposals received from CDWG, T-Mobile, AT&T, Coquina, and Verizon. Bids from Coquina and Verizon were deemed incomplete. Following evaluation, CDWG was selected as the winning bidder at a total cost of $53,478.32, with the district responsible for $10,695.00.

This bid includes both equipment and service, ensuring high-speed 5G connectivity for students and operational enhancements for the Transportation Department. Approval of this item will allow the district to proceed with implementation, expanding learning opportunities beyond the classroom while improving fleet management capabilities.

E-rate funding will be requested to fund the project.  The District will request that e-rate pay 80% of the project and the district’s portion is 20% which will be covered by the technology plan.
Approve a purchase from Pangea Network for an amount not to exceed 53,478.32  pending E-rate funding approval.

Title: b. Seal of Biliteracy Award & Resolution

fields.Content:
The Seal of Biliteracy is an award given by a school district to recognize high school graduates who have attained proficiency in English and one or more additional languages. The purpose of the Seal is to acknowledge and celebrate the value of multilingualism, encourage the study of world languages, and validate the hard work of students who achieve biliteracy. Earning this distinction provides students with a valuable credential for college admissions, scholarship opportunities, and future employment in a global workforce.

By adopting the Seal of Biliteracy, Grandview C-4 School District demonstrates its commitment to recognizing the linguistic and cultural assets of our students and preparing them for success in an increasingly interconnected world.

The accompanying resolution formally establishes the Seal of Biliteracy within the Grandview C-4 School District and outlines the district’s commitment to supporting students in achieving this recognition.
Approve the implementation of the Seal of Biliteracy for the Grandview C-4 School District, beginning on March 21, 2025 and adopt the accompanying resolution in support of this initiative.

Seal of Biliteracy Sponsor Stipend - pay range $4,938 - $6,173  There are minimal costs associated with program implementation, assessments, and recognition that will be absorbed through existing resources and budgets.

The District’s Insurance Committee, Grandview 10 and Grandview 8 worked with CBIZ to negotiate the renewal for medical and dental insurance.  This year, CBIZ conducted a request for proposal process for all lines of benefit coverages for the District.  These results were presented to the Insurance Committee and Grandview 10 and Grandview 8; they then finalized their recommendations regarding the employee insurance proposal on March 11, 2025.  A combined Insurance Communiqué (ATT #1) was issued on March 17, 2025 to all employees for ratification by the employee associations. A plan comparison chart for the medical insurance (ATT #2) and a rate comparison chart for medical insurance (ATT #3) were distributed with the Insurance Communiqué. Online ratification ballots were due at noon on March 20, 2025.  Both the certified and classified employee groups ratified the proposed package.

The joint recommendation can be found it attachment 1 (ATT 1) Highlights include:

Dental Insurance – Delta Dental, with a 4.9% increase (ATT 4)
Life and AD&D Insurance – Standard, with no plan or rate changes
Long Term Disability Insurance – New York Life, with a 4.76% decrease
Vision (voluntary) – Superior vision by Met life, with a .3% decrease (ATT 5)

Health Insurance: Blue Cross Blue Shield (current provider)
  1. The District can renew the current Blue Cross Blue Shield plans, with IRS required change to QHDHP plans, at a 2% increase to the current premiums – for both the District and employee contributions.
  2. The two core plans available to employees will remain – the Blue Select Spira Care Qualified High Deductible Health Plans (QHDHP) utilizing the Blue Select Plus Exclusive Provider Organization (EPO) network.
  3. There will continue to be four buy-up options – the QHDHP utilizing the Preferred Care Blue PPO Network, two PPO (Preferred Care Blue) plans and one HMO (Blue Care) plan.
  4. For those employees who elect Employee Only coverage on Blue Select Plus Spira Care QHDHP EPO II plan, the district will contribute to their individual Health Savings Account (HSA) in an amount equal to the premium difference between this plan and the core Blue Select Plus Spira Care QHDHP EPO I plan ($29.58 per month for 2025-2026).
  5. The District wellness fund is increasing from $90,000 to $95,000 for 2025-2026 plan year.
  6. A comparison sheet is attached highlighting the benefits under each option and the premiums for each plan at each level of coverage.

Approve the recommendation of Grandview 8 and Grandview 10 to renew the Blue Cross Blue Shield Health Insurance with a 2.0% increase and Delta Dental, Standard, and New York Life insurance policies at the proposed rates for the 2025-2026 year.
